vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: asana
Version: 1.0.2

The Asana skill bundle is a standard API integration for managing workspaces, projects, and tasks. It implements a clear authentication flow using either Personal Access Tokens (PAT) or OAuth, storing credentials locally in the user's home directory (~/.openclaw/asana/). The code (asana_api.mjs, oauth_oob.mjs) interacts exclusively with official Asana endpoints (app.asana.com) and lacks any indicators of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: This Asana skill is mostly purpose-aligned, but it has real credential-handling and live-data mutation risks that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Network access to Asana and Asana credentials are proportionate for the integration, but search-tasks forwards arbitrary flags into the Asana request URL, so a direct --token or related secret flag can be unnecessarily placed in URL query parameters.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No postinstall hook, dependency install script, background service, scheduler, or tool replacement behavior was found; the artifact ships local Node scripts and documentation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions disclose PAT/OAuth setup and local storage paths, but they under-disclose that the stored files contain sensitive secrets and show setup flows that pass PATs, client secrets, and authorization codes as command-line arguments.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent auth storage under ~/.openclaw/asana is expected for an API integration, but PATs, OAuth client credentials, and OAuth tokens are written as plaintext JSON without explicit owner-only file or directory permissions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to manage Asana through the REST API, and the read/write commands match that purpose, but it can create, update, complete, and comment on live Asana tasks without a confirmation or dry-run safeguard.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving the skill access to your Asana account and letting it modify live tasks. Prefer environment variables or a secret manager over saved plaintext files, avoid passing secrets on the command line, restrict permissions on ~/.openclaw/asana, and use a low-privilege Asana token or test workspace when possible.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: Credential use is expected for an Asana API skill; artifact inspection showed PAT/OAuth credentials are used for authentication rather than unrelated credential harvesting.
[AE1] unexpected: The referenced oauth_oob.mjs file was present and fully inspected, so the partial-inspection concern did not hold for this adjudication.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The disclosure-gap concerns were partly supported: the docs list credential storage and mutating commands, but do not clearly warn about sensitive local token files, command-line secret exposure, or live Asana writes.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill metadata declares Node and a primary environment variable but does not provide a tight permissions or endpoint scope, which matters because the scripts handle secrets and remote writes.
[RA2] expected: Session persistence through saved PAT/OAuth tokens is purpose-aligned for an Asana integration, but the plaintext storage and file-permission handling increase user risk.
[T09] unexpected: Static scan concerns were verified in the artifacts: credential files are written without restrictive modes, docs encourage secret-bearing command arguments, and search-tasks can include authentication flags in the request URL.
